focus: Screenshots as a pre-structured flow model
noveltyJustification: All six findings were new to this lineage: the screenshot corpus layout, the filename-encoded transitions, the 341-image scale, the sk-vision tool contract and the absent Product Owner image routing had not been recorded before.
ruledOut: Reading every screenshot in the corpus

findings.label: The screenshot corpus is already a flow model on disk: Flow/<platform> holds ordered steps and Components/<platform> holds reusable states; Change Location has 7 step images across Desktop and Mobile plus 6 component images.
sources: Product Context/a — Screenshots/Barter Managed/Dashboard/Flows/Change Location/Flow/Desktop/Dashboard - Click_ Location Selector.png

findings.label: Screenshot filenames encode the trigger and the post-state in prose, so a flow folder yields node labels and transition intents before any pixel read.
sources: Product Context/a — Screenshots/Barter Managed/Dashboard/Flows/Change Location/Flow/Mobile/Sheet - Menu - Locations - Click_ Location.png

findings.label: Scale makes screenshot intake a selection problem: the corpus holds 341 PNGs, so one flow folder rather than the library is the unit of work.
sk-vision is the only local pixel reader for a text-only model: 13 sk_vision_* tools, no API key or cloud upload, opt-in and idle by default, with a one-time Bun build required.
Product Owner has no Figma, screenshot or diagram routing: its bootstrap names one skill, sk-product-owner, and its boundaries cover backlog and doc artifacts only.

Screenshot intake needs a new handler that selects one Flow/<platform> folder, OCRs only labels and target elements, and emits nodes from filenames plus grounded OCR, because no existing Product Owner surface consumes images.
